description: Structured eval definitions for the CloudFront KeyValueStore Deployer. Five-case proven set exercising the READY_TO_DEPLOY / PREREQUISITES_MISSING classification across KVS use cases (A/B testing with Functions integration, feature flags, IP allowlist, wrong runtime, over-size store). Each eval maps to a prompt file and a baseline (no-skill) file for with-skill-vs-baseline comparison.

eval_cases.name: A/B testing KVS with CloudFront Functions integration
eval_cases.branch: READY_TO_DEPLOY — KVS for A/B testing, cloudfront-js-2.0 function, KVS-function linkage, viewer-request event, eventual consistency acknowledged
eval_cases.prompt: Create a CloudFront KeyValueStore named ab-testing-kvs for A/B testing. I need a CloudFront Function named ab-test-router that reads the KVS to route traffic between variant-a and variant-b based on a percentage stored in the KVS. The distribution is E1234567890ABC. I want to change the split without redeploying the function. Account ID: 123456789012. Tags: Environment=production, UseCase=ab-testing.
eval_cases.expected_output:
KVS_DEPLOYMENT: ab-testing-kvs (arn:aws:cloudfront::123456789012:key-value-store/abc-123)
VERDICT: READY_TO_DEPLOY
CHECKLIST:
  [✓] KVS store: ab-testing-kvs — created
  [✓] Store size: ~200 bytes / 1 MB
  [✓] Key count: 4 keys
  [✓] Key schema: kebab-case with ab- prefix
  [✓] Use case: A/B testing
  [✓] Function name: ab-test-router
  [✓] Function runtime: cloudfront-js-2.0 (REQUIRED for KVS)
  [✓] Function stage: LIVE (published)
  [✓] KVS-function link: associated via --key-value-store-associations
  [✓] Distribution: E1234567890ABC — viewer-request event
  [✓] Write path: CLI (put-key for traffic-split changes)
  [✓] etag handling: re-fetch before each write
  [✓] Propagation: eventual consistency acknowledged
  [✓] Tags: Environment=production, UseCase=ab-testing
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws cloudfront-keyvaluestore describe-key-value-store --kvs-arn arn:aws:cloudfront::123456789012:key-value-store/abc-123
  aws cloudfront-keyvaluestore list-keys --kvs-arn arn:aws:cloudfront::123456789012:key-value-store/abc-123
  aws cloudfront describe-function --name ab-test-router
  aws cloudfront get-distribution-config --id E1234567890ABC

eval_cases.prompt: Create a CloudFront KeyValueStore named ip-blocklist-kvs for blocking specific IPs at the edge. I need to block 192.168.1.10, 10.0.0.5, and 172.16.0.3. eval_cases.name: Operator uses cloudfront-js-1.0 runtime (no KVS support)
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — function created with cloudfront-js-1.0 which does not support cf.openKvs(); must update to cloudfront-js-2.0
eval_cases.prompt: I have a CloudFront Function named edge-router that I created with the cloudfront-js-1.0 runtime. I want to read from a KeyValueStore inside it using cf.openKvs(). The KVS is named config-kvs. It's attached to distribution E111111111AAA. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
KVS_DEPLOYMENT: config-kvs
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Function runtime: edge-router is cloudfront-js-1.0 — cf.openKvs() does NOT exist in this runtime. Update the function to cloudfront-js-2.0 and republish.
  [✗] Function stage: Must be LIVE after runtime update. Verify with publish-function.
  [✗] KVS-function link: Must associate config-kvs with edge-router via --key-value-store-associations during the update.
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws cloudfront describe-function --name edge-router --query 'FunctionSummary.FunctionConfig.Runtime'
  aws cloudfront-keyvaluestore describe-key-value-store --kvs-arn <config-kvs-arn>

eval_cases.name: Operator wants 8000 IPs in KVS (exceeds 1 MB limit)
eval_cases.branch: PREREQUISITES_MISSING — 8000 IPs at ~50 bytes each = ~400 KB keys + ~50 bytes each value = ~520 KB, but function iteration over 8000 keys exceeds function execution limits; also approaches store size; recommend WAF IP sets
eval_cases.prompt: I want to store a blocklist of 8000 IP addresses in a CloudFront KeyValueStore. Each IP is about 20 characters. I need the function to check each incoming request against all 8000 entries. Create a KVS named big-blocklist-kvs. Account ID: 123456789012.
eval_cases.expected_output:
KVS_DEPLOYMENT: big-blocklist-kvs
VERDICT: PREREQUISITES_MISSING
CHECKLIST:
  [✗] Store size: 8000 entries × ~50 bytes each = ~400 KB — within 1 MB, BUT iterating 8000 keys per request exceeds the 1 ms function execution limit. Use AWS WAF IP sets for large IP lists (native CIDR support, instant propagation, 10000+ entries).
  [✗] Function execution time: CloudFront Functions have a 1 ms max execution time. Iterating 8000 KVS keys per request is not feasible. Use exact-match key lookups (kvs.get) for small lists only.
  [✗] Alternative: AWS WAF IP sets handle 10000+ entries with native CIDR matching and near-instant propagation. Recommended for this use case.
VERIFICATION_COMMANDS:
  aws wafv2 list-ip-sets --scope CLOUDFRONT
  aws cloudfront-keyvaluestore describe-key-value-store --kvs-arn <arn>
